checked_public_sources.source: Zhang, Xu & Chen (2012), The Exact Likelihood Ratio Test for Equality of Two Normal Populations
checked_public_sources.result: Primary-source confirmation that equality of two independent normal populations admits exact finite-sample likelihood-ratio treatment.

checked_public_sources.source: Hsu, Kakade & Zhang (2012), A tail inequality for quadratic forms of subgaussian random vectors
checked_public_sources.result: Quadratic-form concentration used to bound the pooled variance term in the analytic t-channel power certificate.

checked_public_sources.source: Tian & Ramdas (2021), Online control of the familywise error rate
checked_public_sources.result: Online fallback can recycle significance after a rejection while strongly controlling online FWER. For first-alarm change detection this does not solve pre-alarm late-start alpha dilution, because there is no legitimate prior rejection from which to recycle before the first alarm.

derived_results.claim: A zero-extra-state terminal Gaussian sentinel closes the unbounded KL>=1 power tail for the first H=48/T0=700 start without randomized radial shells.

details.offsets_covered: all integer x=0..16 because the complete alignment gap is excluded
sentinel_tests: two-sided pooled Student t mean test
details.state_cost: no new individualized state if candidate count/mean/SSE are already retained

derived_results.scope: All Gaussian Q=N(mu,r), both mean signs, D_KL(Q||N(0,1))>=1 for the first start. Analytic reductions/concentration but constants are float64, not directed-rounding interval verified.

derived_results.claim: Increasing a fixed sentinel PFA share buys only a finite number of early KL=1 starts because the summable start weights pi_k decay; this is a useful hybrid, not a full late-start replacement.

engineering_screen.method: Dense r-grid plus optimized Hsu weighted-chi-square t-miss bound; engineering screen only, not the formal piecewise certificate.

derived_results.interpretation: At beta=0.09, the coarse screen suggests eta≈0.08 covers about the first three starts, eta≈0.15 about the first four, and eta≈0.20 about the first five; late starts still decay.

derived_results.claim: Online-FWER fallback/recycling is not the missing late-start mechanism for a first-alarm detector.
derived_results.reason: The published fallback improvement reallocates alpha after a rejection. In change detection the first rejection is already the alarm whose PFA is being controlled, so no pre-alarm rejection wealth exists to recycle. A nonshrinking late-start solution must instead share evidence/capital across starts inside a valid e-process or use another first-event-safe construction.

candidates_new.mechanism: Spend a small fixed PFA fraction on exact terminal Gaussian sentinel tests for the first few materialized starts, retaining the existing e-process/future-tail channel for indefinitely late starts. This replaces expensive randomized unbounded radial power certificates where the sentinel applies without pretending summable fixed-time testing can stay nonshrinking forever.
candidates_new.confidence: high for first-start mechanism; medium for optimal eta/number of early starts until start-index-aware formal certificates and joint end-to-end detector accounting are closed.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: Continue randomized Gaussian radial shells indefinitely until all KL>=1 is covered.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Deprioritized. The own r76 shell-to-1.25 artifact showed anchor counts increasing outward despite lower failure rates, while r77 now gives an analytic unbounded-tail route for the first start.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: A terminal fixed-time sentinel with one constant alpha level can cover every future start under global PFA.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Rejected. Without a different shared-capital construction, first-event FWER/PFA requires the per-start fixed-time error spending to be summable, so thresholds shrink with start index.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: Online fallback alpha recycling removes that shrinkage before a change alarm.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Rejected for this use. Its extra allocation is earned after a rejection; the first rejection is already the event whose false-alarm probability must be controlled.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: The 9-state Gaussian bank is now fully adoption-grade.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Not yet. The analytic sentinel has only a formal first-start KL>=1 certificate, constants are not interval verified, and later starts still require the existing e-process/future-tail mechanism or a new capital-sharing proof.

frontier: Derive a start-index-aware formal KL floor I_floor(k,eta) for the terminal Gaussian sentinel under the actual pi_k sequence; use piecewise monotonic envelopes rather than the current dense-grid engineering screen.

Search for or derive a first-event/PFA-valid shared-capital construction that turns repeated terminal Gaussian sufficient-statistic evidence into one e-process without per-start fixed alpha shrinkage; ordinary rejection-based online-FWER recycling is insufficient before the first alarm.

If no such capital-sharing construction closes, formalize the hybrid: exact sentinel for a finite early prefix of starts and the existing future-tail e-process for all later starts, then optimize eta against SNML threshold penalty and state/power savings.
Replace float64 quantiles, KL roots and monotonic partition endpoints in the first-start sentinel certificate with directed-rounding/interval verification.

Repeat only the minimal necessary full-floor certification for I_floor=0.5 and 0.25 after the I=1 hybrid architecture is settled; do not generalize Gaussian evidence to heavy tails/non-Gaussian changes.
exact_next_action: For eta in a small design set, solve the formal piecewise first-event miss bound as a function of start index k and information floor I, and identify the Pareto point between finite early-start coverage and the added SNML threshold log(1/(1-eta)). In parallel attempt a conditional e-value/product-or-mixture construction on terminal block sufficient statistics; require supermartingale/e-process validity under overlapping starts before treating it as a late-start replacement. If overlapping dependence blocks conditional validity, switch to a disjoint-block sentinel substream or retain the existing future-tail e-process. Then interval-verify the selected design constants.
